title: Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch
subtitle: A boy looks for another world
summary: Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch is Level-5's role-playing adventure, first released for PlayStation 3 in Japan on 17 November 2011. Oliver travels to another world hoping to save his mother, accompanied by the fairy Drippy. A story rooted in grief opens into colourful towns, strange creatures and a wider struggle against dark powers. Studio Ghibli produced the animated sequences, while Joe Hisaishi contributed to the score. The world connects the appearance of an animated film with an adventure that gives the player time to explore its places.
body: Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch is Level-5's role-playing adventure, first released for PlayStation 3 in Japan on 17 November 2011. Oliver travels to another world hoping to save his mother, accompanied by the fairy Drippy. A story rooted in grief opens into colourful towns, strange creatures and a wider struggle against dark powers. Studio Ghibli produced the animated sequences, while Joe Hisaishi contributed to the score. The world connects the appearance of an animated film with an adventure that gives the player time to explore its places.

Battles let Oliver and his companions move around an encounter while choosing attacks, spells and defensive actions. Familiars offer another way to participate: the player can train and develop creatures with different strengths, then bring them into the fighting. Their abilities make building a group a continuing part of the journey rather than a decision made only when a new human companion arrives. Recovering resources and choosing when to switch actions remain important, so the friendly presentation accompanies a system that asks the player to learn how the party works.

Oliver's journey begins on foot and later gains other forms of travel, including a boat and a dragon. Those changes turn distant parts of the world map into places the party can finally reach. Towns provide smaller requests and encounters between the larger events, keeping Oliver's wish connected to people he meets along the way. Written by Akihiro Hino, the PlayStation 3 game expanded the earlier Japanese Nintendo DS adventure. Western releases arrived in 2013, and later versions brought its story and world to further platforms.
story_headings: A boy looks for another world
Travel gives the story its scale
